newsitem.title: JAPAN: Nintendo surges on bargain hunting, strong sales.
newsitem.headline: Nintendo surges on bargain hunting, strong sales.

text.p: Shares of Nintendo Co Ltd surged on Wednesday on the Osaka Securities Exchange (OSE) due to bargain hunting and positive sentiment resulting from encouraging sales of its new game software in the United States, traders said.
By 0523 GMT, Nintendo was up 120 yen at 9,320 in trade on the first section of the bourse.
Retailers sold a record 300,000 copies of Nintendo's new Star Fox 64 video game in its first five days, executives of a U.S. unit of the video game maker said on Tuesday.
At a suggested retail price of $69.95, that represents an opening week "box office" take of nearly $21 million, the equivalent of a top Hollywood movie.
Nintendo of America executive vice president Peter Main said in an interview he expected sales to top 800,000 units, or nearly $56 million, by the end of August.
"Positive sentiment has emerged, because in the case of Nintendo buying factors related to new releases had been absent for quite a while," an official at a second-tier brokerage said.
